items.title: Ukraine: Ceasefire holds for its first 30 hours in occupied Oleshky
items.description: A local ceasefire in the Russian-occupied southern Ukrainian city of Oleshky held through its first day and night, despite continued fighting between Moscow and Kyiv elsewhere. The truce, which began on Tuesday in the devastated city, is expected to remain in place until Sunday. Emerald Maxwell reports.

items.title: At least 10 dead in crash between 2 trains in Spain
items.description: A high-speed train slammed into the rear of another train that had stopped, derailing two cars and killing at least 10 people on Wednesday in central Spain, authorities said.

items.title: Ahead of EU-Canada summit, European leaders clash over terminology
items.description: European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen's offer of EU associate member status to Canada has angered both Paris and Berlin. Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney faces criticism over the proposal at home.

items.title: Elderly women and children survive Russian attack on Kharkiv
items.description: A Russian drone attack in Ukraine's Kharkiv late Tuesday forced elderly women and children to evacuate their homes.

items.title: Ceasefire extended across Ukraine's Kherson region, officials say
items.description: The truce was originally planned for the stranded residents of Oleshky, and Russia and Ukraine say no breaches have been reported.

items.title: 'Get Killed Or Starve': Life Under Russian Occupation In Oleshky
items.description: Residents fleeing Russian-occupied Oleshky describe hunger, soaring food prices, and threats from Russian soldiers. Cut off from supplies, civilians risk mines and drone attacks to escape. Now, a proposed cease-fire could open a humanitarian corridor for those still trapped in the Ukrainian city.

items.title: Kiev, 'la tregua a Oleshky durerà fino alle 23 di domenica'
items.description: "Ogni sforzo di de-escalation di questo tipo avvicina la pace tanto attesa in Ucraina"

items.title: World News in Brief: ‘No safe place in Ukraine’, IAEA calls for Iran nuclear inspections, Kenya hosts thousands of Ethiopians fleeing clashes
items.description: The UN refugee agency (UNHCR) on Tuesday urged continued international support for Ukraine’s population as Russian airstrikes intensify and humanitarian needs grow in advance of another bitterly cold winter.

items.title: Israelis abroad flock home for ‘most important election we’ve ever had’
items.description: Democracy. The Hamas attack. Wars in Gaza, Lebanon, and Iran. Netanyahu’s long tenure. For Israelis returning home to vote, the list of momentous issues is long.

items.title: Why Ukraine may be involved in Mali's conflict
items.description: Allegations that Ukrainian specialists are supporting Tuareg rebels in Mali highlight Kyiv's effort to challenge Russian influence far beyond the battlefield in Europe.

items.title: ‘Still Just a Child’: The Russian Teenagers Fighting and Dying in Ukraine
items.description: A growing number of Russian soldiers who were still schoolchildren when the full-scale invasion of Ukraine began are being killed in the war.

items.title: Russia Says Ukraine Peace Talks Won’t Slow War, Open to Local Truces
items.description: Russia says upcoming US-brokered peace talks will not slow its war against Ukraine but signals openness to local humanitarian truces. The Kremlin’s stance comes as a ceasefire is planned for Russian-occupied Oleshky to allow aid deliveries and civilian evacuations.
